t: You're on Judd Street, in the London Borough of Camden. The street is named after Andrew Judde, also spelled Judd, a sixteenth-century English merchant who became Lord Mayor of London. He lived from 1492 to 1558, and he was knighted on the fifteenth of February 1551. So the name on the street sign belongs to a Tudor-era City merchant who rose to the capital's highest civic office.
